title: Finish tying a pre-wrapped necktie
instruction: Thread the wide end through the front loop, tighten and fit the knot to the collar, then release both hands.
context: Tying a necktie is a familiar dressing skill and a useful example of assistance for someone with limited hand movement.
setup: A reversible woven polyester tie, 1.45 m long, with pointed ends, 70 mm wide end, 35 mm narrow end, 1.2 mm effective thickness and 37.55 g mass. Pale and gold edge markings make twists visible; either face can face out. A rigid plastic collar form has a 110 mm-diameter, 100 mm-high neck, a 162 mm lower rim and 60 mm-high collar flaps with an open front. Its neck centre is (0.400, 0, 1.250) m on the YAM table (height 0.7475 m). A rigid plastic stand with a 455 × 25 × 25 mm post, 210 × 25 × 25 mm rear arm and 180 × 160 × 12 mm base supports it. A dark centre mark shows the front. The tie starts around the collar with one loose front wrap already prepared. Its opening is approximately 120 by 90 mm, centred 130 mm below the collar. The left fingers hold the wide end 90 mm from its free tip, which hangs above the opening; the right fingers hold the outer band, with the narrow blade routed inside the wrap. The wide tip has not passed through the front loop, and no completed knot is present. The screenshot and fixed reset specify this experimenter-prepared layout. Lengths are measured below the neck form at z=1.200 m. The YAM fingers have smooth convex covers, approximately 94 × 72 × 68 mm in each finger link frame. The supplied scene and fixed reset specify the exact geometry and drape.
scoring: 0.5 for a genuine necktie knot retained after both hands release for 5 seconds. Increase this to 1.0 if the knot is centred within 20 mm horizontally, the neckband gap is at most 15 mm, the wide blade hangs flat without an axial half-twist, the narrow end is behind it with its tip at least 10 mm higher, and the wide tip hangs 350–440 mm below the collar’s lower edge. No retained knot gives zero. Fabric damage, visible material passage, undisclosed support or artificial tightening gives zero.
run_limit: 3,600 control steps (180 seconds at 20 Hz), including the final 5-second released hold.
reset_notes: Restore the pre-wrapped but unthreaded layout and starting grasps shown in the setup image. Fixed cloth and robot initial conditions settle for 5 seconds with ordinary holding actions and the shared contact model. Both policies use exactly this reset. Threading, tightening, fitting and release must happen during the trial.
fidelity: Native FEM models reversible cloth, gravity, bending and self-contact; tearing is not modelled. Smooth convex finger covers avoid collision seams. Geometric compliant grip captures enclosed cloth within a closing 30 mm gap, retains 9.4 mm minimum joint clearance and releases above 40 mm. A 10 mm rear-collar contact approximates static friction. Cover mass is neglected; slip forces are uncalibrated. Both policies share this model, without a target knot or automatic tightening.
scores: Not evaluated. No demo or Dream score exists.
